abstract: Near-infrared genetically encoded calcium ion (Ca2+) indicators (NIR GECIs) enable Ca2+ imaging at longer wavelengths than green or red fluorescent GECIs, providing reduced autofluorescence and phototoxicity, and improved compatibility with deep-tissue and multiplexed imaging applications. We have previously reported biliverdin (BV)-binding phytochrome-based NIR GECIs such as NIR-GECO2G that exhibit inverse fluorescence responses. Although inverse response GECIs can effectively report Ca2+ dynamics, their high baseline fluorescence in the resting apo state causes faster photobleaching and substantial out-of-focus background fluorescence, complicating signal interpretation. Here, using the inverse response NIR-GECO2G as the starting scaffold, we developed a direct response Ca2+ indicator, designated dNIR-GECO1.0, through iterative rounds of protein engineering and screening. dNIR-GECO1.0 exhibited greater molecular brightness than NIR-GECO2G, robust fluorescence in mammalian cells without exogenous BV supplementation, and a high dynamic range for reporting Ca2+ changes. A detailed mechanistic investigation identified the key mutations within the Ca2+ binding domain that were necessary to convert the inverse response indicator into a direct response indicator. Resonance Raman spectroscopic analysis provided insight into the specific changes in the BV chromophore resulting from the Ca2+-dependent conformational change.
